creator: Alexander Terp
description:
On 2026-09-28 at 22:25:50Z (0.11.0, Alex's Mac, window 98894), the tunnel supervisor's once-a-second `ssh -O check` did not return within `CONTROL_WITHIN` (2s). The supervisor ended the master 100ms later and opened a new one. All seven devenv panes lost their bridges, and the four on screen were dead for 15s, 14s of it waiting on a retry (a_2YQD5xCFq).

The master was very likely working. `-O check` is answered locally and never touches the network (`crates/muster-ssh/src/tunnel.rs:468`), and pane p27bs5f62b painted every second up to 22:25:50. A second window (pid 42509) held its own master to the same host through that second and never logged `tunnel.down`. Load average was about 7 on 8 performance cores. The log does not say why this one check took over 2s.

`-O check` fails in two ways that mean different things:

- It fails at once, because no socket is there or nothing answers on it: the master is gone, and reopening at once is right.
- It times out: something still holds the control path and did not answer in 2s. One timeout is enough to end it today (`supervise`, tunnel.rs:314-363).

A timeout never means the network dropped. A master whose connection dies exits when ServerAlive gives up, and the next check then fails at once. So a timeout is a master that is slow or wedged, and asking again on the next poll before ending it costs a wedged master about 3s and a slow one nothing.

From `~/Library/Logs/muster/muster-2026-09-28_16-30-31-98894.jsonl`:

    22:25:50.723Z  tunnel.down           the master on .../muster-98894-devenv.ctl did not answer `-O check` within 2s
    22:25:50.815Z  bridge.stream.lost x7 the daemon hung up
    22:25:50.839Z  tunnel.master_ended
    22:25:51.814Z  tunnel.reopened
    22:25:52.313Z  tunnel.reverse
title: 🔌 One slow -O check ends an ssh master that is carrying every pane
